resume.summary: Sample summary. Two to four sentences that connect the candidate's experience to the target role: years of experience and core strengths such as **project coordination** and **process improvement** first, then the kind of problems they solve, then the value they would bring to the team.

items.heading: Project Coordinator
bullets: Sample bullet: start with an action verb, say what was done, and end with a measurable result, for example "cut report turnaround from **[5] days to [2]**".
Coordinated a **cross-functional team** of [n] people across [n] workstreams, keeping delivery on schedule and within budget.
Introduced a [process or tool] that improved [metric] by **[x%]**; replace with a verified achievement.
Keep each bullet to one or two lines; three to five bullets per role is usually enough.

items.heading: Operations Assistant
bullets: Maintained [type of] records for [n] accounts with [x%] accuracy, supporting monthly reporting.
Streamlined the [name] workflow by documenting each step and removing duplicate approvals.
Trained [n] new team members on internal tools and procedures.

items.heading: Customer Service Representative
bullets: Resolved an average of [n] customer enquiries per day across phone, email and chat.
Proposed an FAQ update on [topic] that reduced repeat enquiries.

items.heading: Operations Dashboard (sample project)
items.description: One sentence on what the project is and who it helps.
bullets: Built with [tools]; describe your role and the measurable outcome, such as **[n] hours saved** per month.

items.heading: Bachelor of Science in [Field of Study]
bullets: Relevant coursework, thesis title or capstone project (optional).

items.heading: Volunteer Coordinator
bullets: Organised [n] community events with teams of up to [n] volunteers.

paragraphs: Sample opening paragraph. Name the role, **Project Coordinator**, and say in one or two sentences why this company and this role interest you.

Sample middle paragraph. Connect two or three achievements from the resume to the job description, for example how you **coordinated a team of [n] people** or **cut turnaround time by [x%]**. Keep it specific and measurable, and avoid repeating the resume word for word.
Sample closing paragraph. Restate your interest, mention your availability for an interview, and thank the reader for their time. The whole letter should fit on one page.
